summary: ansible-core 2.19 templating changes: set_fact no longer turns 'yes'/'no'/'true'/'false' strings into booleans (use the bool filter), template lookup convert_data has no effect (use from_json), _-prefixed attributes are blocked, templates always render natively and None stays None, embedded inline templates warn or fail, allow_unsafe_lookups is gone, range() must go through a filter, and bad #jinja2: overrides are errors.
questions: Why is my set_fact 'yes' string no longer a boolean?
Why does my template return None instead of an empty string?
Why do nested {{ }} templates fail in ansible-core 2.19?

answer_card.title: set_fact no longer converts yes/no strings
answer_card.answer_md:
Templates always render in Jinja2 native mode now, so `set_fact` keeps strings such as `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"true"` and `"false"` as strings. Use native YAML booleans where you define the variable, or convert explicitly:

```yaml
- set_fact:
    enabled: "{{ some_string | bool }}"
```
